hints: Resolve vertically for equilibrium to find the normal reaction $R$: $R + 5\sin\alpha = mg$.
Resolve horizontally to find the friction force $F = 5\cos\alpha$, then apply limiting equilibrium $F = \mu R$.
walkthrough:
From $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, identify the ratios from a 3-4-5 right-angled triangle:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6,\quad \cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$$

First calculate the downward gravitational weight of the 0.8 kg particle ($W = mg$):
$$W = 0.8 \times 10 = 8\text{ N}$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation. The normal contact force $R$ and the upward component of the 5 N pull balance the downward weight:
$$R + 5\sin\alpha = W$$

Subtract $5\sin\alpha$ from both sides to solve for $R$:
$$R = 8 - 5(0.6) = 8 - 3 = 5\text{ N}$$

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation. The maximum friction force $F$ balances the forward pull:
$$F = 5\cos\alpha = 5(0.8) = 4\text{ N}$$

Use the friction law in limiting equilibrium ($F = \mu R$) and rearrange by dividing by $R$ to solve for $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$$

hints: Recalculate the normal reaction $R$ with the pulling force increased to $10\text{ N}$: $R + 10\sin\alpha = 8$.
Calculate the new friction force using $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = 0.8$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $10\cos\alpha - F = ma$, and solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
The pulling force is now increased to 10 N. Set up the vertical force balance to find the new normal reaction $R$:
$$R + 10\sin\alpha = W \implies R = 8 - 10(0.6) = 8 - 6 = 2\text{ N}$$

Calculate the new kinetic friction opposing motion using $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = 0.8$:
$$F = 0.8 \times 2 = 1.6\text{ N}$$

Calculate the forward pulling component:
$$F_{\text{forward}} = 10\cos\alpha = 10(0.8) = 8\text{ N}$$

Subtract friction from the forward pull to find the resultant force accelerating the particle:
$$F_{\text{net}} = F_{\text{forward}} - F = 8 - 1.6 = 6.4\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) and divide both sides by mass $m = 0.8\text{ kg}$ to find acceleration $a$:
$$6.4 = 0.8 \times a \implies a = \frac{6.4}{0.8} = 8\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
